headline: Lower medical costs lift profit; full-year outlook raised
summary_short: UnitedHealth earned $4.56 per share ($4.69 adjusted) on revenue of $112.7B; earnings from operations rose 53% y/y to $6.6B as the medical care ratio improved to 88.4% from 89.9%.
summary_long: Revenue was flat y/y. UnitedHealthcare earned $2.8B (margin 3.3%) on benefit changes, pricing discipline and cost management; Optum earned $3.7B (margin 5.6%), with Optum Health revenue down 10% on fewer value-based care patients. The medical care ratio fell to 88.4%, including $610M of favorable reserve development; the operating cost ratio was 12.8%. Cash flow from operations was $5.1B and debt-to-capital 41.7%. Year to date UNH repurchased $5.0B of stock and paid $6.2B in dividends. Full-year 2026 outlook was raised to at least $19.50 EPS and at least $20.50 adjusted.
confidence_notes: The shard's EPS of $4.69 is the company's adjusted EPS; GAAP EPS was $4.56 per the release. Net medical reserve development of $610M related to 2026 dates of service flattered the medical care ratio. Prior-year adjusted EPS is derived from the resolver's y/y comparison basis ($2.59 SEC basic EPS), which is a GAAP figure, so the +81% adjusted-EPS y/y delta mixes bases and should be read as indicative only. Guidance prior range not stated in the release text read.

drivers.explanation: UnitedHealthcare revenue fell to $86.3B from $87.1B on membership and product mix changes; Optum Health revenue fell 10% on fewer value-based care patients, partly offset by growth in Optum Insight and Optum Rx.
Driven by disciplined execution across UnitedHealthcare and Optum, including benefit changes, pricing discipline and medical and operating cost management.
Medical cost management initiatives, benefit design changes, pricing discipline and care delivery enhancements; included $610M of net favorable prior period reserve development.
Realized operating efficiencies, partially offset by accelerating investments in technology, processes and people.
CEO Stephen Hemsley cited discipline and execution across the business; the company raised its full-year 2026 outlook to adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share.
